RHABDOMYOLYSIS.label_snippet: Cases of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis with acute renal failure secondary to myoglobinuria have been reported with HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, including atorvastatin.

HEPATIC ENZYME INCREASED.label_snippet: Increases in serum transaminases (AST or ALT) to greater than 3 times ULN on 2 or more occasions occurred in 0.7% of patients in clinical trials.

ACUTE PANCREATITIS.label_snippet: Not documented in warnings or adverse reactions.

pubmed_articles.title: Statin-induced acute pancreatitis: A systematic review of pharmacovigilance data.

assessment.executive_summary: Pharmacovigilance surveillance for Atorvastatin identified established labeled signals for Rhabdomyolysis and Hepatic Enzyme Elevation, along with a statistically significant unlabeled signal for Acute Pancreatitis.

signals.clinical_note: Expected class effect; well-documented in FDA package insert.
Transaminase elevations monitored routinely in clinical practice.
Unlabeled signal meeting Evans criteria; corroborated by published literature (PMID 28372605).

assessment.detailed_findings: Analysis of FAERS post-marketing reports for Atorvastatin confirms expected musculoskeletal and hepatobiliary safety signals. Rhabdomyolysis demonstrates a marked reporting disproportionality (PRR 43.32, ROR 48.12, Chi² 468,200), consistent with established HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor class warnings. Transaminase increases are also elevated (PRR 8.75). Crucially, Acute Pancreatitis emerged as an unlabeled statistical signal (PRR 2.87, 95% CI 2.70-3.04, Chi² 1420.8), warranting continued periodic surveillance.
assessment.clinical_recommendation: Maintain vigilance for muscle symptoms and liver function; note prospective literature associations regarding rare drug-induced pancreatitis.
assessment.limitations: FAERS data consists of voluntary spontaneous submissions subject to notoriety bias, underreporting, and duplicate reporting. These figures represent statistical associations and cannot calculate incidence rates or establish medical causality.
assessment.disclaimer: Educational demonstration only. Not intended for individual clinical decision making.
